result.markdown: --- title: "[vals.fmt_time()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Format values as times. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/great-tables/blob/main/great_tables/_formats_vals.py#L1335-L1407){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python vals.fmt_time(x, time_style="iso", pattern="{x}", locale=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Format input values to time values using one of 5 preset time styles. Input can be in the form of `time` values, or strings in the ISO 8601 forms of `HH:MM:SS` or `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS`. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [X]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of values to be formatted. [time_style]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [TimeStyle]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["iso"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The time style to use. By default this is the short name `"iso"` which corresponds to how times are formatted within ISO 8601 datetime values. There are 5 time styles in total and their short names can be viewed using `info_time_style()`. [pattern]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["{x}"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : A formatting pattern that allows for decoration of the formatted value. The formatted value is represented by the `{x}` (which can be used multiple times, if needed) and all other characters will be interpreted as string literals. [locale]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : An optional locale identifier that can be used for formatting values according the locale's rules. Examples include `"en"` for English (United States) and `"fr"` for French (France). ::: ## Formatting With The `time_style` Argument {.doc-formatting-with-the-timestyle-argument} We need to supply a preset time style to the `time_style` argument. The time styles are numerous and can handle localization to any supported locale. The following table provides a listing of all time styles and their output values (corresponding to an input time of `14:35:00`). | | Time Style | Output | Notes | |----|---------------|---------------------------------|---------------| | 1 | `"iso"` | `"14:35:00"` | ISO 8601, 24h | | 2 | `"iso-short"` | `"14:35"` | ISO 8601, 24h | | 3 | `"h_m_s_p"` | `"2:35:00 PM"` | 12h | | 4 | `"h_m_p"` | `"2:35 PM"` | 12h | | 5 | `"h_p"` | `"2 PM"` | 12h | We can use the `info_time_style()` function within the console to view a similar table of time styles with example output. ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [list[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of formatted values is returned. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#8796b2a8 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from great_tables import vals vals.fmt_time(["05:32:17", "13:01:02"], time_style="h_m_s_p") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ['5:32:17 AM', '1:01:02 PM'] ``` ::: :::
